description_ru: Реставратор обнаруживает в «шедевре» пигмент, которого не могло существовать в XVII веке, и сообщает об этом владельцу галереи.
text:
Victor: Helena, you said on the phone it was urgent. I hope the Vermeer isn't damaged.
Helena: The painting is fine, Victor. It's the painting that worries me. Please sit down.
Victor: That sounds ominous.
Helena: When I removed the old varnish from the lower left corner, I found a pigment that shouldn't be there. Synthetic ultramarine. It wasn't invented until the early nineteenth century.
Victor: And Vermeer died in 1675.
Helena: Precisely.
Victor: Surely a previous owner could have cleaned it badly and left a modern trace behind?
Helena: A cleaner might add varnish, Victor, but nobody sprinkles a nineteenth-century pigment through the paint itself. It is mixed into the original layers.
Victor: Could it be a later restoration? Somebody touching up a damaged patch?
Helena: That was my first thought, so I took samples from three further areas. The same pigment appears in the sky, in the woman's sleeve, even under the signature.
Victor: Under the signature?
Helena: Which means the signature was added after the blue, not before. A forger's mistake, and a rather careless one.
Victor: Helena, I bought this painting from a respected dealer in Geneva. It has papers, a provenance, an entry in a catalogue from 1934.
Helena: Papers can be forged as easily as paintings. And catalogues can be mistaken, or deliberately misled. I'm not accusing anyone, I'm telling you what the chemistry says.
Victor: What happens if I do nothing?
Helena: Then you'd be knowingly selling a forgery, which is a crime, and I'd be obliged to document my findings. I'm sorry, but my reputation rests on honesty.
Victor: No, no, I'm not asking you to hide anything. I'm merely trying to understand how much of my money has evaporated.
Helena: Possibly all of it, I'm afraid. Although a skilful fake from the right period can have a value of its own, as a historical curiosity.
Victor: A curiosity. Wonderful. I paid four million for a curiosity.
Helena: There's another route. Let me contact an independent laboratory, quietly, to confirm the results. If they agree, you'll have grounds to pursue the dealer.
Victor: And if they don't?
Helena: Then I'll happily eat my words, and the varnish, if you like.
Victor: Do it. But Helena, until then, not a word to anyone.
Victor: How long will the tests take?
Helena: Ten days, perhaps two weeks. In the meantime I'd keep the painting in storage and away from any buyers who might be circling.
Victor: There is one, as it happens. A collector from Singapore, very keen.
Helena: Then tell him you need time for conservation. It will even be true.
Victor: Of course. Discretion is the other half of my profession.
Helena: That was my line, but I'll allow it.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Верхние зубы касаются нижней губы, звук звонкий; не заменяйте на «в» с губно-губным оттенком или «ф».
Долгий звук: губы округлены, язык слегка отведён назад; не сокращайте и не превращайте в «о».
Ударение: ˌultramaˈrine (побочное на первом, главное на последнем), disˈcretion, ˌindeˈpendent.

questions.question: What did Helena find under the varnish?
questions.answer: A synthetic pigment, ultramarine, that did not exist in Vermeer's time.

questions.question: Where else does the pigment appear?
questions.answer: In the sky, the woman's sleeve and under the signature.

questions.question: How much did Victor pay for the painting?
What does Helena propose to do next?
questions.answer: Contact an independent laboratory to confirm the results.
